对每条相关命中，报告：编号、标题、状态(open/closed)、是否 merged（PR）、日期、要点。重点找与"第一个 builtin 无法执行 / renew / index 0"相关的条目。

      "body": "examples/xedge_demo: Add Xedge IoT Toolkit with BAS integration\r\n    \r\n    Add support for Xedge, an embedded software toolkit for IoT applications\r\n    using Lua scripting with HTTP(S), WebSockets, MQTT, and device I/O.\r\n    \r\n    * netutils/xedge: Dependency manager that downloads BAS library\r\n     and BAS-Resources, generates XedgeZip.c during build\r\n    \r\n    * examples/xedge_demo: Complete example showing Xedge integration\r\n     with HTTP server, Lua runtime, and SNTP time synchronization\r\n\r\n## Summary\r\n\r\nI'm supporting @surfskidude to update xedge support with nuttx.\r\n\r\nThis commit covers conversations: \r\nhttps://github.com/apache/nuttx/pull/16352\r\nhttps://github.com/apache/nuttx-apps/pull/3071\r\n\r\n## Impact\r\n\r\n``xedge_demo`` a lightweight Lua-based web framework for building secure, real-time IoT applications\r\n=========================================================================\r\n\r\n`Xedge <https://realtimelogic.com/products/xedge/>`_ is a robust IoT and web framework that is designed for microcontrollers. It is based on the industrial-grade Barracuda Application Server, designed for seamless OEM integration. Xedge accelerates embedded firmware development by providing a flexible, Lua-based environment and a full stack of industrial-strength protocols, including:\r\n\r\n- OPC UA\r\n- Modbus\r\n- MQTT\r\n- SMQ\r\n- WebSockets\r\n- HTTP/HTTPS\r\n\r\nThis Xedge port for NuttX comes pre-configured and requires:\r\n\r\n- TCP/IP v4 and v6 support\r\n- File System support\r\n- 2 MB RAM allocated statically in ``xedge/xedge_main.c``\r\n\r\n.. note::\r\n   These instructions set up Xedge in **development mode**. Xedge supports many configuration options that differ between development and production builds. For production settings and optimization, refer to the general Xedge build instructions (details below).\r\n\r\nWhy Use Lua and Xedge in Embedded Systems\r\n------------------------------------------\r\n\r\nGreat Lua developers don't treat it as a \"better C\"; they treat it as a complement. Lua is an extension language, which means it's designed to work alongside C, not replace it. Smart embedded programmers use C for performance-critical, low-level code and Lua for high-level business logic, such as processing sensor data and managing secure cloud connectivity.\r\n\r\nWriting embedded business logic purely in C often means hundreds of lines of boilerplate code to manage memory, handle complex APIs, and handle errors. Lua, especially when paired with a framework like Xedge, lifts that burden. It provides high-level libraries and modules out of the box for protocols, networking, file systems, and more.\r\n\r\nThis shift doesn't just make development easier; it makes it faster. What used to take weeks in C can now be done in days. Lua's simplicity encourages rapid prototyping and quick iteration, which is essential in modern IoT and embedded development, where both time-to-market and security are critical. For a conceptual overview of why this hybrid development model is so powerful, check out the tutorial `Why Smart C Coders Love Lua.\r\n\r\n## Testing\r\n\r\nRun xedge example with qemu-armv8a board\r\n\r\n```bash\r\n $ ./tools/configure.sh qemu-armv8a:xedge_demo\r\n $ make\r\n```\r\n\r\nRunning with QEMU:\r\n\r\n```bash\r\n   $ qemu-system-aarch64 -cpu cortex-a53 -smp 4 -nographic \\\r\n     -machine virt,virtualization=on,gic-version=3 \\\r\n     -chardev stdio,id=con,mux=on -serial chardev:con \\\r\n     -global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false \\\r\n     -netdev user,id=u1,hostfwd=tcp:127.0.0.1:8080-10.0.2.15:80,hostfwd=tcp:127.0.0.1:8443-10.0.2.15:443,hostfwd=tcp:127.0.0.1:10023-10.0.2.15:23 \\\r\n     -device virtio-net-device,netdev=u1,bus=virtio-mmio-bus.0 \\\r\n     -mon chardev=con,mode=readline -kernel ./nuttx\r\n```\r\n\r\nRunning Xedge in NuttX terminal\r\n\r\n```bash\r\n   nsh> xedge_demo\r\n    [    3.020000] [CPU0] Error: cannot set root to /mnt/lfs\r\n    [    3.020000] [CPU0] Installing DiskIo failed!\r\n    [    3.070000] [CPU0] Xedge: Server listening on IPv4 port 80\r\n    [    3.080000] [CPU0] Xedge: SharkSSL server listening on IPv4 port 443\r\n    [   13.720000] [CPU0] Xedge: Received invalid browser localStorage\r\n    [   20.090000] [CPU1] 10.0.2.2 GET \"rtl/assets/favicon.ico\" t\r\n    [   20.090000] [CPU1] Mozilla/5.0 (X11;       "body": "## Summary\r\n\r\nnshlib/[cd|ls|pwd]: add support for local CWD(Current working directory)\r\n\r\nThis PR will still allow basic shell operations such as cd/ls/pwd to be used even when the environment is disabled.\r\n\r\nSigned-off-by: chao an <anchao@lixiang.com>\r\n\r\n## Impact\r\n\r\nDepends on: https://github.com/apache/nuttx/pull/15120\r\n\r\n## Testing\r\n\r\nsim/nsh  and enable  CONFIG_DISABLE_ENVIRON\r\n\r\nbefore:\r\n```\r\n$ ./build/nuttx \r\n\r\nNuttShell (NSH) NuttX-10.4.0\r\nnsh> ls\r\nnsh: ls: missing required argument(s)\r\nnsh> cd\r\nnsh: cd: command not found\r\nnsh> pwd\r\nnsh: pwd: command not found\r\nnsh> ls /\r\n/:\r\n bin/\r\n data/\r\n dev/\r\n etc/\r\n proc/\r\n tmp/\r\nnsh> \r\n```\r\nafter:\r\n\r\n\r\n```\r\n$ ./build/nuttx \r\n\r\nNuttShell (NSH) NuttX-10.4.0\r\nnsh> ls\r\n/:\r\n bin/\r\n data/\r\n dev/\r\n etc/\r\n proc/\r\n tmp/\r\nnsh> cd\r\nnsh> cd /data\r\nnsh> pwd\r\n/data\r\nnsh> ls /\r\n/:\r\n bin/\r\n data/\r\n dev/\r\n etc/\r\n proc/\r\n tmp/\r\nnsh> \r\n\r\n```",

      "body": "Build Rust applictions with cargo is the most commn way, and it's more easy to cooporate with Rust ecosystem.\r\n\r\nThis example shows how to use cargo to build a simple hello world application.\r\n\r\nAnd please notice that you need to install nighly version of rustc to support this feature, any version after https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/127755 is merged, can use NuttX as cargo target directly.\r\n\r\nBuild\r\n-----\r\n\r\nTo build hello_rust_cargo application, you can use any target that based on RISCV or ARM, for example:\r\n```\r\ntools/configure.sh rv-virt:nsh\r\n```\r\n\r\nAnd disable ARCH_FPU in menuconfig, since the hard coded target triple in this demo is `riscv32imac`.\r\n\r\nTODO\r\n-------\r\n1. ~~Add support for Rust in CMake based system~~\r\n2. ~~Upstream https://github.com/no1wudi/libc to rust-lang/libc~~\r\n3. ~~Port libstd of Rust to NuttX, which blocked by 2.~~\r\n\r\nUPDATE\r\n---------\r\n\r\nNow you can just enable the example on many ARM/RISCV platform, build system will handle target triple for Rust.\r\n\r\n",

      "body": "## Summary\r\nAn important feature of ELF binaries for NSH is the capability to replace built-in applications with updated ELF applictions on a file system.  This works because of this ording in NSH:\r\n\r\n- Load file from file system if possible\r\n- If not, run built-in application if possible\r\n- If not, run NSH command line command if possible\r\n- If not, report that the command was not found\r\n\r\nThis critical behavior was broken by this commit:\r\n\r\n    commit 9a28ccf836c1b9f0eb5e1163964042eddc207697\r\n    Author: chao.an <[REDACTED-INTERNAL-EMAIL]>\r\n    Date:   Fri Feb 21 09:54:47 2020 +0800\r\n\r\n        nsh/parse: try the builtin configuration first\r\n\r\n        In the case of enable the BUILTIN_APPS/FILE_APPS at the same time,\r\n        try the builtin list first to ensure that the relevant configuration\r\n        (stacksize, priority) can be set normally.\r\n\r\nThis commit breaks the feature because it changes the order to that the built-in application is tried first.  Hence, the version on the file system will never replace the built-in version.\r\n\r\nThat commit must be reverted in order to restore the correct functionality.\r\n\r\n## Impact\r\n\r\nNone other than the ruined feature should become functional again.\r\n\r\n## Testing\r\n\r\nUnder test by floweh@gmx.net. ### Add system init
Refer to the implementation of Android Init Language, consists of five broad classes of statements: Actions, Commands, Services, Options, and Imports.

Actions support two types of triggers: event and action. Action triggers also support runtime triggering. Services support lifecycle management, including automatic restart (at specified intervals), and starting/stopping individually or by class. Import supports files or directories, and we may add a static method in the future. The following are some differences:
  1. The Android Init Language treats lines starting with `#` as comments, while we use a preprocessor to handle comments.
  2. For action commands, we can omit "exec" and directly execute built-in apps or nsh builtins.
  3. Regarding the property service, users can either adapt it by self or directly use the preset NVS-based properties.
  4. Only part of standard action commands and service options are implemented currlently.

To enable system/init:
  ```diff
  -CONFIG_INIT_ENTRYPOINT="nsh_main"
  +CONFIG_INIT_ENTRYPOINT="init_main"
  +CONFIG_SYSTEM_INIT=y
  ```

For format and additional details, refer to: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/system/core/+/master/init/README.md

### Add class start/stop for service
Usage:
```
      class_start <classname>
      class_stop <classname>
```

### Add NSH builtin support for action
Enable `CONFIG_SYSTEM_SYSTEM` to support nsh builtins, which depends on nsh.

### Warning for long commands
If the command of an action takes too long (greater than `CONFIG_SYSTEM_INIT_ACTION_WARN_SLOW` milliseconds, 50 ms by default), a warning log will be output for analysis and debugging.

For example:

### Add exec_start support for action
Format: `exec_start <service>`

Start the specified service and pause the processing of any additional initialization commands until the service completes its execution. This command operates similarly to the `exec` command; the key difference is that it utilizes an existing service definition rather than requiring the `exec` argument vector.

This feature is particularly intended for use with the `reboot_on_failure` built-in command to perform all types of essential checks during system boot.

### Add reboot_on_failure for service
Add support for the reboot_on_failure option to the service.

When the execution of a command within a certain action fails (returning a non-zero status code), init will continue to execute subsequent commands or actions and will not proactively terminate the startup process. To implement the functionality of "terminating the startup process after a command execution fails", there are two methods:
1. Execute conditional statements (if/then/else/fi) via exec command, but this depends on sh:
   ```
   on init
       exec -- set +e; \
               mount -t fatfs /dev/data /data ; \
               if [ $? -ne 0 ] ; \
               then \
                 echo "failed" ; \
                 reboot ; \
               else \
                 echo "succeed" ; \
               fi;
   ```
2. Via service's oneshot + reboot_on_failure:
Although the example uses sh, it does not depend on it and can be replaced with any other Builtin Apps.
   ```
   on init
       exec_start mkdir_tmp
       ls /tmp

   service mkdir_tmp sh -c "mkdir /tmp"
       reboot_on_failure 0
       oneshot
   ```

      [    8.060000] [ 3] [ 0] init_main:   +flag 'restarting'
    > [    8.060000] [ 3] [ 0] init_main: Error reboot on failure of service 'console' reason 0
  ```

###  Add boot support for action

Add support for booting a new application firmware image, depends on `BOARDCTL_BOOT_IMAGE`.
When the built-in boot command of nsh is enabled, the built-in boot command of Init will take precedence (see init_builtin_run()). To use the built-in boot command of nsh, use: `exec -- sh boot [args...]`.
Referred to nshlib/nsh_syscmds.c: cmd_boot()

### Handle trailing file '\0'

When `ETC_ROMFS` is disabled to reduce the bin size, we can provide the init.rc file via a pseudo-file in the boards/vendor directory. For example:
  ```diff
  - CONFIG_ETC_ROMFS=n
  - CONFIG_PSEUDOFS_FILE=y
  - CONFIG_DISABLE_PSEUDOFS_OPERATIONS=n
  ```
  ```C
  FAR const char *init_rc =
    "on init\n"
    "    start console\n";
    "service console sh\n"
    "    restart_period 100\n";

  int fd = open("/etc/init.d/init.rc", O_WRONLY | O_CREAT);
  /* ... */
  ssize_t n = write(fd, init_rc, strlen(init_rc) + 1);
  /* ... */
  close(fd);
  ```

The last character '\0' in the file content will be treated as a new line, and the number of parsed parameters will be zero (abnormal, there should be at least one keyword)

### Parse default cpu-specific configs

On the basis of init.rc, add default parsing of cpu-specific configs.
- /etc/init.d/init.rc
- /etc/init.d/init.cpu${CPUID}.rc

Refactor function `init_parse_configs()` to parse files from the default path instead of identifying and parsing directories or files, as the functionality is unnecessary.

## Impact
The newly added component can be used for user space system initialization and daemon process management.

      "body": "### Description / Steps to reproduce the issue

I am using the `CONFIG_RAMLOG_SYSLOG` feature (log messages being sent to `/dev/kmsg` and retrieved via `dmesg`). This works in general.
But sadly the output of `dmesg` is usually heavily garbled: lots of characters (single or in big chunks) are missing. Repeated calls of `dmesg` emit different output (i.e. the missing characters are randomly spread).

# Potential cause

The output of `dmesg` is created by [`nsh_catfile`](https://github.com/apache/nuttx-apps/blob/5585c9d347ccc0d14b909eb8a8e0e74ad81bb04e/nshlib/nsh_fsutils.c#L143).
`nsh_catfile` uses the [`nsh_write`](https://github.com/apache/nuttx-apps/blob/5585c9d347ccc0d14b909eb8a8e0e74ad81bb04e/nshlib/nsh_console.h#L48) macro:

```c
#define nsh_write(v,b,n)        (v)->write(v,b,n)
```

I tried to slow down the read operation in `nsh_catfile`:
```patch
diff --git a/nshlib/nsh_fsutils.c b/nshlib/nsh_fsutils.c
index 878c1d18e..f3d91d2bc 100644
--- a/nshlib/nsh_fsutils.c
+++ b/nshlib/nsh_fsutils.c
@@ -178,7 +178,7 @@ int nsh_catfile(FAR struct nsh_vtbl_s *vtbl, FAR const char *cmd,

   for (; ; )
     {
-      int nbytesread = read(fd, buffer, IOBUFFERSIZE);
+      int nbytesread = read(fd, buffer, 8);

       /* Check for read errors */
```

The above change fixes the issue for me. No more characters get lost in the void.

The above change is obviously not acceptable.
Instead, the output should probably block in some way in order to prevent itself from being overwhelmed?

      "body": "examples/xedge_demo: Add Xedge IoT Toolkit with BAS integration
    
    Add support for Xedge, an embedded software toolkit for IoT applications
    using Lua scripting with HTTP(S), WebSockets, MQTT, and device I/O.
    
    * netutils/xedge: Dependency manager that downloads BAS library
     and BAS-Resources, generates XedgeZip.c during build
    
    * examples/xedge_demo: Complete example showing Xedge integration
     with HTTP server, Lua runtime, and SNTP time synchronization

## Summary

I'm supporting @surfskidude to update xedge support with nuttx.

This commit covers conversations: 
https://github.com/apache/nuttx/pull/16352
https://github.com/apache/nuttx-apps/pull/3071

## Impact

``xedge_demo`` a lightweight Lua-based web framework for building secure, real-time IoT applications
=========================================================================

`Xedge <https://realtimelogic.com/products/xedge/>`_ is a robust IoT and web framework that is designed for microcontrollers. It is based on the industrial-grade Barracuda Application Server, designed for seamless OEM integration. Xedge accelerates embedded firmware development by providing a flexible, Lua-based environment and a full stack of industrial-strength protocols, including:

- OPC UA
- Modbus
- MQTT
- SMQ
- WebSockets
- HTTP/HTTPS

This Xedge port for NuttX comes pre-configured and requires:

- TCP/IP v4 and v6 support
- File System support
- 2 MB RAM allocated statically in ``xedge/xedge_main.c``

.. note::
   These instructions set up Xedge in **development mode**. Xedge supports many configuration options that differ between development and production builds. For production settings and optimization, refer to the general Xedge build instructions (details below).

Why Use Lua and Xedge in Embedded Systems
------------------------------------------

Great Lua developers don't treat it as a "better C"; they treat it as a complement. Lua is an extension language, which means it's designed to work alongside C, not replace it. Smart embedded programmers use C for performance-critical, low-level code and Lua for high-level business logic, such as processing sensor data and managing secure cloud connectivity.

Writing embedded business logic purely in C often means hundreds of lines of boilerplate code to manage memory, handle complex APIs, and handle errors. Lua, especially when paired with a framework like Xedge, lifts that burden. It provides high-level libraries and modules out of the box for protocols, networking, file systems, and more.

This shift doesn't just make development easier; it makes it faster. What used to take weeks in C can now be done in days. Lua's simplicity encourages rapid prototyping and quick iteration, which is essential in modern IoT and embedded development, where both time-to-market and security are critical. For a conceptual overview of why this hybrid development model is so powerful, check out the tutorial `Why Smart C Coders Love Lua.

      "body": "## Summary

* interpreters/python: Enable Python's socket module

Enables the Python's socket module. This allows applications to be built to interact with POSIX-compatible sockets, which is supported by NuttX.

## Impact

Allows application to use system's sockets within Python interpreter. Once accepted, I will update the `rv-virt:cpython` defconfig on NuttX's repository and provide a proper documentation on how to use it.

      "body": "## Summary
Add pipeline support for nsh commandline through `pipe2()` and `posix_spawn_file_actions_adddup2()`
1. Pack parameters of nsh_execute() as struct nsh_exec_param_s
    - Input redirect flags currently is hardcode, passing by arguments maybe better.
    - Only support redirect to path_name, redirect to fd is needed for pipeline.
2. Add pipeline support for commandline
3. Concat variable arguments failed - [nshlib/pipeline: Concat variable arguments failed](https://github.com/open-vela/nuttx-apps/pull/18/commits/fec5af6a1e28089be4cc5b9df45c10affa80b382)
    - Without this patch
    ```
    nsh> set var_test `uname`
    nsh> echo $var_test
    NuttX
    nsh> echo $var_test | cat
    sh [5:100]
    
    nsh>
    ```
    - With this patch
    ```
    nsh> set var_test `uname`
    nsh> echo $var_test
    NuttX
    nsh> echo $var_test | cat
    sh [4:100]
    NuttX
    nsh>
    ```
    Reported by @jasonbu and @[REDACTED-INTERNAL-EMAIL], thank you ;-)

And nesting pipeline supported.

## Impact
nsh: nsh_parse_command()

## Testing
#### General
```
# Redirectin
cat < /etc/init.d/rc.sysinit

# Pipe
ls | cat

# Pipe (nested)
ls | cat | cat | cat

# FIFO
mkfifo /dev/testfifo
cat /dev/testfifo &
ls > /dev/testfifo

# CMDPARAMS
set name `uname`
echo $name

# binfmt/sotest
sotest
```
#### With dd
Depends: https://github.com/apache/nuttx-apps/pull/2751
```bash
# Env

mount -t hostfs -o fs=. /data 
ls | cat | dd | cat | dd of=/data/test_dd_stdin

#Read from stdin and write to stdout
ls | cat | dd | cat | dd
```

检索完成。以下为最终报告。

## 命中列表（按相关度排序）

### apache/nuttx-apps（官方上游）

1. **PR #3168** — "nshlib/nsh_builtin.c: Add support to run builtin dirrectly without creating a separate thread" — **closed / merged**（merged 2025-09-11；创建 2025-08-27，作者 wangchdo）
   要点：引入新配置 `CONFIG_NSH_BUILTIN_AS_COMMAND`，让 builtin app 像普通 NSH 命令一样直接运行而不创建独立线程。这是唯一与 `builtin_isavail` 相关的命中（命中来自评论讨论 builtin->main 与 nsh_cmd_t handler 的区别及 hook 位置），但**不是**修复 index 0 误判。

2. **PR #3167** — 同标题 — **closed / 未合并**（2025-08-27 关闭）
   要点：#3168 的前身/重复提交，未合并。

3. **PR #255** — "apps/nshlib: Restore correct load order for binaries" — closed / merged（2020-05-17）
   要点：恢复 NSH 命令解析顺序（文件系统 app → builtin → NSH 命令）。与 builtin 执行顺序相关，但与 index 0 无关。

4. **PR #80** — "Make.defs: Fix to exclude loadable apps from builtin app list" — closed / merged（2020-02-20）
   要点：loadable app 不应出现在 builtin 列表。与 builtin 表构造相关，无关 index 0。

5. **PR #2885** — cd/ls/pwd local CWD — closed / merged（2024-12-11）。要点：正文含 "command not found" 字样，无关。
6. **PR #2522** — sh -c 替换 pthread detach — closed / merged（2024-10-21）。要点：内存泄漏修复，无关。
7. **PR #3120** — Xedge 示例 — closed / merged（2025-07-25）。无关。
8. **PR #2487** — Rust cargo 示例 — closed / merged（2025-01-10）。无关。
9. **Issue #3063** — nsh_catfile 输出乱码 — open（2025-04-22）。无关。

### open-vela（注：仓库名实为 `open-vela/nuttx-apps`，不存在 `open-vela/apps`；open-vela/apps 查询返回 422 即因仓库不存在）

10. **PR #18** — "Add pipeline support for nsh commandline" — closed / merged（2025-01-10）。无关。
11. **PR #76** — osperf 编译警告修复 — closed / merged（2025-02-27）。无关。
12. **PR #55** — 移除 --param 编译选项 — closed / merged（2025-01-22）。无关。
13. **PR #93** — "Add system init" — closed / 未合并（draft，2025-10-23→2025-12-04 stale 关闭）。无关。
    - `repo:open-vela/nuttx-apps builtin_isavail` 搜索结果为 **0 条**；整个仓库仅约 4 个 open issues。

## 代码现状佐证（关键）

- **apache/nuttx-apps master** 的 `nshlib/nsh_builtin.c` 当前直接调用三参数版 `exec_builtin(cmd, argv, param)`，已无 `builtin_isavail()` + `if (index > 0)` 代码。
- **open-vela/nuttx-apps dev** 分支的同一文件与上游一致，同样无该逻辑。
- 文件提交历史（2013–2026）中：历史上存在 `builtin_isavail(cmd)` 调用的时期，判断条件一直是 `index >= 0`（返回 -1 表示不存在），**从未出现过 `if (index > 0)` 的判断**，因此也从未有过针对它的修复提交。

## 结论

**官方尚无该问题的报告或修复，且该 bug 在上游/OpenVela 公开代码中不存在。**

- 在两个官方仓库（apache/nuttx-apps、open-vela/nuttx-apps）中均未检索到任何 issue/PR 报告"builtin 表第 0 项无法通过 NSH 执行"、"builtin_isavail 返回 0 被 `if (index > 0)` 误判"、或"第一个 builtin / renew 无法执行"的问题。
- 上游代码历史中 NSH 对 `builtin_isavail()` 的用法是 `>= 0`（0 即有效索引，第 0 项可正常执行）；现版本已改为直接 `exec_builtin()`，不存在该误判路径。
- 唯一值得留意的相关条目是 **PR #3168（merged）**：新增 `CONFIG_NSH_BUILTIN_AS_COMMAND`，改变了 builtin 的执行方式（直接在 NSH 线程中调用 `builtin->main()`，不创建子线程），并引入了相应的解析顺序变化。若你们遇到的"第 0 项无法执行"出现在启用该配置或移植该改动之后，建议对照该 PR 排查；但它本身并非针对 index 0 的修复。
- 该 bug 很可能出自某个下游内部 fork（如小米 Vela 闭源分支）的二次修改，尚未上报到官方 GitHub。
